mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and electrolyte wasting (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), while dorzolamide is renally eliminated and can worsen hypokalemia through carbonic anhydrase inhibition, increasing risk of renal dysfunction and hypokalemic complications.
action: Monitor renal function, electrolytes (particularly potassium and magnesium), and blood pressure closely during concurrent use; consider alternative topical glaucoma agents if amphotericin B therapy is prolonged.
